hints: Focus on how the units of Kc come from the concentrations in the Kc expression, remembering that solids are never included.
Write the Kc expression for equation 1 first, noting that C(s) is left out so you have one concentration on top and two on the bottom.
Compare top minus bottom moles for each equation to see which ones give a net power of -1, which is what mol^-1 dm^3 means.
walkthrough:
**Recall how Kc units work**

Think of each aqueous concentration as having units of $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$. The overall units of $K_c$ just come from multiplying and dividing those units.

Rule to use:
$$\text{units of } K_c = (\text{mol dm}^{-3})^{\Delta n}$$
where $\Delta n$ = (moles of aqueous or gaseous products) - (moles of aqueous or gaseous reactants). Solids are omitted.

**Check equation 1**

Equation 1 is $\text{A(aq) + B(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{C(s) + D(aq)}$. The solid C is not in the $K_c$ expression.

Expression and units:
$$K_c = \frac{[\text{D}]}{[\text{A}][\text{B}]}$$
$$\text{units} = \frac{\text{mol dm}^{-3}}{(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^2} = \text{mol}^{-1}\text{dm}^{3}$$
So 1 is correct.

**Check equation 2**

Equation 2 is $\text{P(aq) + Q(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{R(aq)}$. All species are included.

Expression and units:
$$K_c = \frac{[\text{R}]}{[\text{P}][\text{Q}]}$$
$$\text{units} = \frac{\text{mol dm}^{-3}}{(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^2} = \text{mol}^{-1}\text{dm}^{3}$$
So 2 is also correct.

**Check equation 3 and conclude**

Equation 3 is $\text{W(aq) + 2X(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Y(aq) + Z(aq)}$.

Expression and units:
$$K_c = \frac{[\text{Y}][\text{Z}]}{[\text{W}][\text{X}]^2}$$
$$\text{units} = \frac{(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^2}{(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^3} = \text{mol}^{-1}\text{dm}^{3}$$
So 3 is also correct. Since 1, 2 and 3 all work, the correct choice is the one that includes all three.

options.A: Correct because all three equations give units of mol^-1 dm^3. Each has one more concentration term on the bottom of Kc than on the top, giving (mol dm^-3)^-1.
options.B: Incorrect because it leaves out equation 3. Students choose this if they miscount the moles in W + 2X <=> Y + Z and think 3 moles on the left and 2 on the right gives different units, forgetting it is 2 versus 3 concentration terms.
options.C: Incorrect because it leaves out equation 1. Students choose this if they wrongly include the solid C(s) in the Kc expression, which would give no units instead of mol^-1 dm^3.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only equation 1. It misses that equations 2 and 3 have the same pattern of one extra reactant concentration, so they must have the same units.
